brief: An aluminium pulley hub. A flange disc 50 mm across and 6 mm thick, with a round hub 25 mm across and 15 mm tall standing on top of it, centred. A 10 mm bore runs through both the flange and the hub. Three 5 mm holes pass through the flange only, equally spaced on a 38 mm circle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

implied: The pulley hub is made of aluminium
stated: A flange disc 50 mm across and 6 mm thick
A round hub 25 mm across and 15 mm tall standing on top of it
A 10 mm bore runs through both the flange and the hub
Three 5 mm holes pass through the flange only, equally spaced on a 38 mm circle
intent.summary: An aluminium pulley hub with a flange disc and a round hub, both centered on a 50 mm diameter flange disc. The hub has a 10 mm bore and three 5 mm holes through the flange only, equally spaced on a 38 mm circle. It carries no load.
unstated: The magnitude and direction of the load on the pulley hub

note: requirements: the record as the run accepted it. The answer is the designer's, returned identically twice: a flange disc and a hub, each cylinder's origin written as its centre so the hub floats 4.5 mm above the flange; a bore and two of the three 5 mm holes naming nothing to cut; the two holes at the centre, drilled sideways; the 38 mm circle declared as `hole_spacing` and read by nothing.

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X and REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Y at 50 mm: the brief calls the part square or round at its largest stated size, and nothing in the requirement set measured the part's size at all. A dimension parameter is declared just as truthfully by a plate 30 by 12 as by a plate 30 by 30, and one was: sixteen claims, every one green, and the plate was 30 by 12.

added REQ_ROUND: the brief calls this part round, and two equal bounding boxes do not say a part is round -- a 25 mm square block has a 25 by 25 box exactly as a 25 mm cylinder does. One run asked for a shaft collar and got a square block with both extent claims passing. This measures the built surface: 1 is a cylinder, a square is 0.707.

added REQ_HOLES_10MM: the brief states 1 open hole of 10 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_5MM: the brief states 3 open holes of 5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.
